summary: Phase 149O.20L.7O.2H.0 (HMIC v1.5 CertificationRecord Contract-Version Closed-Schema Alignment Repair) is complete: HMIC V1.5 CERTIFICATIONRECORD CONTRACT-VERSION CLOSED-SCHEMA ALIGNMENT REPAIRED -- INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION PENDING. Phase 149O.20L.7O.2H reported HMIC-001 v1.5 with a 35-member frozen content/source identity and a 7-member contract-version identity (_CONTRACT_IDENTITY_FILES), but its own production left _CONTRACT_VERSIONS_REQUIRED_KEYS (the separate Wave A CertificationRecord closed-schema acceptance constant consumed by _require_contract_versions) at six members, omitting HBDC-001 -- a gap first surfaced by 149O.20L.7O.2G, reconfirmed by 149O.20L.7O.2G.1, and left deliberately unrepaired by 2H with a 'disclosed, out-of-scope, Wave A vs Wave B' framing. This phase (149O.20L.7O.2H.0) opened finding B-149O.20L.7O.2H-1 and, per its own governing instruction not to assume the repair, first independently re-derived the normative intended relationship from HMIC-001 v1.5's own primary text (HMIC-REQ-032, HMIC-REQ-040, HMIC-REQ-053, HMIC-REQ-067, HMIC-REQ-069, HMIC-REQ-103) before touching production. HMIC-REQ-067 (SS20) states, unambiguously: 'Seven entries, no more, no fewer, as of v1.5.' HMIC-REQ-069 states validation 'SHALL compare each contract_versions entry -- seven entries as of v1.5 -- against the named contract's own current, live version header,' explicitly classing a required contract key absent from a stored record as a mismatch. HMIC-REQ-053 states 'every contract_versions member (HMIC-REQ-067, seven entries) receives both bindings uniformly -- no contract_versions member is exempted from the digest binding.' HMIC-REQ-032 (SS11) defines contract_versions as one field on CertificationRecord; there is no HMIC-001 textual basis anywhere for a narrower 'Wave A closed-schema acceptance set' distinct from Wave B's own derive_contract_versions output -- 'Wave A'/'Wave B' are production-module organizational labels never used as contract vocabulary. This is Outcome A of the governing task's three possible outcomes: the contract already unambiguously requires all seven current contract identities inside CertificationRecord.contract_versions; the contract itself needed no repair, only production conformance. Historical reconstruction (git show on Phase 149O.20D's 5671448a and Phase 149O.20F's d3be5440) confirms the omission originated as an implementation oversight at 149O.20F, which widened only _CONTRACT_IDENTITY_FILES (four to five members) without touching _CONTRACT_VERSIONS_REQUIRED_KEYS (left at four); Phase 149O.20G's own independent verification of that alignment covered only the 5/5-contract Wave B identity, never once referencing _CONTRACT_VERSIONS_REQUIRED_KEYS or _require_contract_versions in its test diff -- the Wave A gap was never independently verified or adjudicated by any phase before this one, only named and carried forward. The defect was demonstrably load-bearing, not cosmetic: before repair, derive_contract_versions's own current seven-member mapping on this repository could never itself parse as a CertificationRecord.contract_versions value (rejected as 'has unrecognized contract entries: [HBDC-001]'), and validate_active_hatp_mandatory_independent_verification_certification's own SS31 step 10 dict-equality comparison (current seven-member derived mapping vs. a stored record's schema-capped six-member value) could never succeed for any stored record, meaning a future real certification ceremony deriving the true seven-member mapping could never store a matching record, and any six-member record it did store would permanently self-fail its own contract-version validation step. Repair: _CONTRACT_VERSIONS_REQUIRED_KEYS widened from six to exactly seven members (added HBDC-001), now exactly equal to _CONTRACT_IDENTITY_FILES's membership; the misleading 'disclosed, out-of-scope, Wave A vs Wave B' comment replaced with one citing HMIC-REQ-067/069/053's own text. No HMIC contract version bump: v1.5 already unambiguously required seven; only production conformance was repaired. One stale, pre-v1.1-era 'the four frozen contracts' own version headers' editorial cross-reference (SS31/HMIC-REQ-103's validation-algorithm-summary text) was corrected to 'the seven bound contracts' own version headers' as a minimal, additive clarification -- not a new normative statement. A textually-identical SS23/HMIC-REQ-076 occurrence was deliberately left untouched: it falls inside the byte-identity window a prior independent-verification phase's own regression guard (tests/test_phase_149o_20l_7l_6_..._independent_verification.py::test_hmic_req_145_closure_paragraph_present_and_unchanged) protects around HMIC-REQ-145's own text, whose regex-based block extraction only stops at the next parenthetical-titled '**HMIC-REQ-NNN (' marker -- HMIC-REQ-076 has no such marker, so the guarded window incidentally spans into its unrelated prose; editing it would fail an unrelated prior phase's own regression check for no compensating benefit, so it is reproduced verbatim, out of this phase's own repair scope. SS11/HMIC-REQ-032's illustrative contract_versions example was widened to show all seven current members (versions marked illustrative, SS20 cited as the authoritative current key set), and its stale '(SS22)' cross-reference corrected to '(SS20)' (SS20, 'Contract Binding Set,' is the section that actually defines the set; SS22, 'Non-Authoritative Repo-Local Signals,' is unrelated). This repair did not disturb the independently reconciled 35/7 alignment, closure limb (d), the three Trust-Enrollment/signing source files, HPSE-001, or HHCE-001 -- byte-for-byte unmodified, confirmed by git diff and by this phase's own focused suite. A new 33-test focused repair suite (tests/test_phase_149o_20l_7o_2h_0_hmic_certificationrecord_contract_version_closed_schema_alignment_repair.py) covers every item of the governing prompt's Section 37 required-test list: exact _CONTRACT_IDENTITY_FILES/_CONTRACT_VERSIONS_REQUIRED_KEYS membership and their equality, derive_contract_versions's expected current membership and successful parsing, missing-HBDC/HPSE/HHCE and unknown-eighth-key rejection, an isolated seven-bound-contract fixture proving the exact seven-member record VALID/wrong-HBDC-version/wrong-HPSE-version/wrong-HHCE-version CONTRACT_MISMATCH cases, certification-ID sensitivity to the mapping, admin-construction round-trip retention of all seven identities, closed-fail behavior for a historical six-member record (now impossible to even construct through the parser), the unchanged 35-file/limb-(d)/runtime state, and the finding-disposition marker in this phase's own canonical document. Six pre-existing test files across the repository whose own literal contract_versions fixtures hardcoded the pre-repair six/seven-member shape (missing HBDC-001) were updated to include HBDC-001, matching the exact same fixture-literal repair pattern this repository's own prior additive-widening phases use; 2H's own focused suite's assertion of the pre-repair six-member behavior was updated in place to assert the now-repaired seven-member state, with its docstring recording the prior claim and pointing at this phase's finding. Repository-wide regression: the full hmic-or-hatp_mandatory_certification pytest -k selection was compared node-for-node against a disposable git-worktree baseline at this phase's own true entry commit 0893f40a (zero shell/comm diff after fixes); the signing_ceremony-or-hardware_credential_admin-or-principal_signer_admin-or-fido2-or-deployment_binding selection was likewise compared and shows zero node-for-node diff beyond expected commit-state-dependent working-tree checks that self-resolve once committed -- hatp_signing_ceremony.py, hatp_fido2_provider.py, hatp_hardware_credential_admin.py, and hatp_principal_signer_admin.py were not touched by this phase; BF-1, BF-2, B-149O.20L.7O.2F.3-1, and B-149O.20L.7O.2F.3-2 remain independently closed, unaffected, not reopened. Fast Green (isolated disposable git-worktree at this phase's own true entry commit 0893f40a, -m fast_green -n auto, compared against current post-commit source in the identical environment): fixed 306 non-passing/8071 passed/7 skipped/12 errors; current 307 non-passing/8103 passed/7 skipped/12 errors. Exact non-passing-node comm diff: one fixed-only node (tests/test_shell_gate.py::TestAuditPersistence::test_verify_detects_tampered_record, a flake that failed only in the fixed-worktree run and is absent from current), two current-only nodes both independently classified non-blocking (a push-state-dependent HEAD-equals-origin-main check that resolves once pushed, and the known shell-gate audit-verify-cli timing flake this repository's own prior phases already diagnosed, independently re-run in isolation and confirmed to pass in 13.14 seconds -- this phase touched zero shell-gate/audit files); zero error-node-set diff (12 both trees). This phase's own new 33-test focused suite contributed 0 failed. Finding B-149O.20L.7O.2H-1 disposition: REPAIRED -- CONTRACT-VERSION RECORD/DERIVATION ALIGNMENT RESTORED -- INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION PENDING -- NOT CLOSED (this phase does not close its own finding; only a future independent-verification phase, 149O.20L.7O.2H.1, may). Finding B-149O.20L.7O.2G-1 retained unchanged: ALIGNED -- 35-MEMBER CONTENT/SOURCE IDENTITY IMPLEMENTED -- 7-MEMBER CONTRACT IDENTITY IMPLEMENTED -- INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION PENDING -- NOT CLOSED. Class-B verifier files, DeploymentBinding admin producer/script, and CBV-S1 remain unaffected and unchanged; CBV-S10 remains OPEN, untouched, no readiness integration wired by this phase. No HMIC certification was created or activated at any point in this phase. No HATP activation, FIDO2 provisioning, real Principal/Signer enrollment, or real DeploymentBinding creation occurred. No hac-dell or Protected Root state was mutated. Runtime remains Observed/observe/unavailable throughout, confirmed via pcae runtime inspect both before and after this phase's changes. Exact production files changed: src/pcae/core/hatp_mandatory_certification.py and docs/contracts/HATP_MANDATORY_INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION_CERTIFICATION_CONTRACT.md only, plus this phase's own focused test suite, six pre-existing test-file fixture repairs, phase documentation, PROJECT_STATUS.md, CHANGELOG.md, and lifecycle/report artifacts -- exactly the expected change scope, no broader.
